edges.notes: Linux kernel is implemented primarily in C (kernel development documentation).
GCC/Clang Unix targets predominantly emit ELF object files and executables.
GCC traditionally drives GNU as and ld on Unix-class GNU toolchains.
Clang may invoke lld when configured (e.g. -fuse-ld=lld) alongside LLVM codegen.
Clang is a major production C/C++ compiler implementation alongside GCC.
GCC is the GNU reference implementation for C and C++ on many platforms.
GDB is the common source-level debugger for C/C++ in GNU/Linux toolchains.
LLDB is a common debugger for C/C++ in LLVM/Clang-centric toolchains.
Hosted C environments on GNU/Linux commonly use glibc as the standard C library implementation.
Hosted C on musl Linux triplets uses musl as the standard C library implementation.
Hosted MSVC C on Windows commonly uses UCRT/VCRUNTIME-class DLLs as the standard C runtime implementation.
Hosted C on FreeBSD uses the FreeBSD base system libc as the standard C library implementation.
Hosted C on OpenBSD uses the OpenBSD base system libc as the standard C library implementation.
Hosted C on NetBSD uses the NetBSD base system libc as the standard C library implementation.
Hosted C on DragonFly uses the DragonFly base system libc as the standard C library implementation.
Hosted C on illumos distributions uses the illumos core libc as the standard C library implementation.
Hosted C on Android uses Bionic as the standard native C library implementation.
Hosted C on many embedded GCC targets uses newlib as the standard C library implementation.
C++ builds interoperate with C via extern C and libc headers; libstdc++ sits above the C library.
C++ with libc++ still relies on the platform C library underneath for hosted C services.
C++ ABI runtime sits above C/POSIX services while supporting compiler-generated C++ machinery.
